assertions.source: Files the qou-oots choice can move, vs the raw grep count that was quoted as the blast radius. These are EXPECTED TO DIFFER -- the assertion records both numbers side by side rather than testing equality; read the values, not the pass/fail.

description: Bean qou-oots option C. Classifies every live (non-_deprecated) computations/ file that references a `w_lambda`-named weight by WHICH family it actually constructs: PLANCHEREL (the dim_q^2/[n]_q!, dim_q^2/D^2 or Molien families -- the ones the qou-oots canonical choice is between), MARKOV (y_lambda, NOT part of that choice), BOTH (a deliberate comparison or an undeclared straddle), or NAME-ONLY (the token appears with no construction -- the files a raw grep over-counts). Purpose is to replace the raw grep count of 43, which was quoted as a blast radius and is the wrong number for it because `w_lambda` names several different objects. LIMITS: classification is by source pattern, so a weight reached through an alias, a factory, or a witness read at runtime is invisible; every bucket is a LOWER BOUND on its own membership and NAME-ONLY is a lower bound on 'computes no weight'. Measured, not complete.

summary.note: The second figure is what the qou-oots canonical choice can move. BOTH is included in it because a file carrying both families is affected whether it is a deliberate comparison or a straddle -- which of those it is has NOT been triaged here.

molien_vs_dimq2_lambda_dependence.note: Ratio w_Molien(lam)/w_dimq2(lam) at the substrate q0, normalised to its own mean over partitions of n. A value of 1.0 everywhere would mean the two families differ by a lambda-INDEPENDENT constant, and every same-n ratio built from them would be invariant. They do not: the spread is large and monotone from the single row to the single column, which is the q^{-kappa} factor. So consumers whose reported quantities are same-n ratios -- which is ALL SIX candidates in beta_ew_delta_I_321_and_wedderburn.py -- are invariant under dim_q^2/[n]_q! -> dim_q^2/D^2 (same numerator) but are NOT invariant under the Molien option.
